title: Functions and Wrappers To Streamline Complex Analytic Workflows in Non-randomized Oncology Database Studies Based On The ENCORE Trial Emulation Project
text: Real-world oncology data often suffers missing values, requiring sophisticated imputation techniques. combined propensity score analyses treatment effect estimation, complexity increases substantially. code: agreement_metrics(   x,   analysis_col,   group_col = NULL,   estimate_label = "HR (95% CI)",   smd_threshold = 1.96,   metrics = c("significance_agreement", "estimate_agreement", "smd_agreement"),   show_aggregate = FALSE,   show_aggregate_total = TRUE,   smd_scale = c("log", "identity", "logit", "cloglog"),   digits = 2 )

title: Calculate Agreement Metrics Between RCT and RWE Results — agreement_metrics
text: x data.frame tibble containing RCT RWE results (wide format, see examples). Must contain columns: rct_estimate = Point estimate RCT rct_lower = Lower confidence limit RCT result rct_upper = Upper confidence limit RCT result rwe_estimate = Point estimate RWE emulation study rwe_lower = Lower confidence limit RWE result rwe_upper = Upper confidence limit RWE result analysis_col Character. Name column identifying different analyses group_col Character. Optional. Name column grouping results (e.g., database) estimate_label Character. Label estimates table header. Default: "HR (95% CI)". value one "HR (95% CI)", "(95% CI)", "RR (95% CI)", table footnote includes matching abbreviation definition (e.g. "HR = Hazard ratio"); value used -header without adding abbreviation definition footnote. smd_threshold Numeric. Threshold SMD agreement; single positive number. Default: 1.96 (alpha=0.05) metrics Character vector. agreement metrics compute display. Must subset "significance_agreement", "estimate_agreement", "smd_agreement". Default: three. Metrics excluded skipped entirely (computed), relevant "smd_agreement" since expensive metric compute may meaningful effect size types. show_aggregate Logical. TRUE, adds summary row bottom table pooled agreement percentage selected metric (Yes / (Yes + ) across rows, excluding "NA" cells, e.g. failed SMD calculations, denominator). Default: FALSE. show_aggregate_total Logical. TRUE, adds source note table single agreement percentage pooled across selected metrics rows combined, using Yes / (Yes + ) logic show_aggregate. Default: TRUE. TRUE, formatted percentage string (e.g. "78% (109/140)") also attached directly returned gt object show_aggregate_total, can accessed programmatically (e.g. result$show_aggregate_total) without parsing back source note text. smd_scale Character. transform apply RCT/RWE estimates confidence limits computing SMD. One "log" (default), "identity", "logit", "cloglog". "log" appropriate ratio-scale measures (HR, , RR, IRR), since confidence intervals constructed via delta method log scale. "identity" skips transform, measures already additive/difference scale (e.g. risk differences). "logit" proportions bounded [0, 1]. "cloglog" log-log transform survival probability, log(-log(p)), scale "log-log" confidence interval method used survival::survfit() (conf.type = "log-log"). Note km_pooling() pools survival probabilities different scale, log(-log(1 - p)) (Morisot et al. 2015), see documentation. option expects inputs particular domain (log: > 0; logit cloglog: strictly 0 1; identity: real number); values outside domain silently produce "NA" SMD agreement result row rather raising error. "cloglog" decreasing function input, lower/upper confidence limits automatically reordered transforming preserve lower-less--upper invariant required internally. See Details related limitation smd_scale address. digits Whole number NULL. NULL, RCT RWE point estimates confidence limits rounded many decimal places agreement metric (significance, estimate, SMD) computed, , example, RWE estimate 0.799 RCT confidence limit 0.80 lead estimate agreement digits = 2. estimates limits displayed many decimals (SMD always shown 2). Estimates must positive interval must satisfy lower <= estimate <= upper, checked rounding. Missing values allowed give "NA" agreement result affected metric. pre-existing smd_value column x recomputed rounded. Default: 2. Set NULL disable rounding.

title: Calculate Agreement Metrics Between RCT and RWE Results — agreement_metrics
text: Calculates three types agreement metrics, controlled via metrics argument: Statistical significance agreement: RCT RWE confidence intervals fall side null value 1 (entirely , entirely , include null, .e. non-significant) Estimate agreement: RWE estimate within RCT confidence interval SMD agreement: Standardized mean difference threshold (default 1.96) Metrics excluded via metrics computed (just hidden output), relevant SMD calculation particular, since expensive step may meaningful effect size types. estimates hazard ratios (HR) must positive. Estimates transformed SMD calculation according smd_scale (log-transformed default). Known limitation non-ratio-scale effect sizes: smd_scale changes transform used inside SMD calculation. change function's ratio-scale assumptions: positivity check rct_estimate/rwe_estimate significance_agreement's comparison null value 1 applied regardless smd_scale. example, setting smd_scale = "identity" use risk difference still requires positive input values still evaluates statistical significance null 1 rather 0 — incorrect difference-scale measure. known, currently unaddressed limitation; agreement_metrics() designed ratio-scale effect measures (HR, , RR, IRR) beyond just SMD calculation.

Simulate a cohort with 500 patients and 20% missing data data <- simulate_data(   n = 500,   imposeNA = TRUE,   propNA = 0.2 )  # Impute the data set.seed(42) mids <- mice(data, m = 5, print = FALSE) #> Warning: Number of logged events: 765  # Fit a propensity score model fit <- as.formula(treat ~ dem_age_index_cont + dem_sex_cont + c_smoking_history)  # Weight patients within each imputed dataset wimids <- weightthem(   formula = fit,   datasets = mids,   approach = "within",   method = "glm",   estimand = "ATO" ) #> Estimating weights     | dataset: #1 #>  #2 #>  #3 #>  #4 #>  #5 #>   # Define a survival model formula cox_fit <- as.formula(survival::Surv(fu_itt_months, death_itt) ~ treat)  # 1) Weighted (wimids) or matched (mimids) object: # weights (and clusters) are set automatically cox_pooling(wimids, surv_formula = cox_fit) #> ℹ Input: <wimids>: weighted datasets extracted with MatchThem::complete(action #>   = "all", all = FALSE, include = FALSE) (m = 5) #> ℹ Fitting Cox proportional hazards model with survival::coxph() in each #>   dataset: #>   formula: survival::Surv(fu_itt_months, death_itt) ~ treat #>   weights = weights (default for the input type) #>   robust = TRUE (derived: weights, cluster or id are used) #>    term  estimate  std.error statistic     p.value  conf.low conf.high #> 1 treat 0.7297697 0.08792742 -3.582799 0.000374082 0.6139819 0.8673933 #>              b       df dfcom       fmi      lambda m         riv        ubar #> 1 4.570604e-05 487.4987   496 0.0111428 0.007094245 5 0.007144933 0.007676384  # code: library(encore.analytics)  library(mice)  library(MatchThem)   # simulate a cohort with 500 patients with 20% missing data  data <- simulate_data(    n = 500,    imposeNA = TRUE,    propNA = 0.2    )   # impute the data  set.seed(42)  mids <- mice(data, m = 5, print = FALSE) #> Warning: Number of logged events: 765   # fit a propensity score model  fit <- as.formula(treat ~ dem_age_index_cont + dem_sex_cont + c_smoking_history)   # weight (or alternatively match) patients within each imputed dataset  wimids <- weightthem(    formula = fit,    datasets = mids,    approach = "within",    method = "glm",    estimand = "ATO"    ) #> Estimating weights     | dataset: #1 #>  #2 #>  #3 #>  #4 #>  #5 #>    # fit a survival model  km_fit <- as.formula(survival::Surv(fu_itt_months, death_itt) ~ treat)   # 1) weighted (wimids) or matched (mimids) object:  # weights (and clusters) are set automatically  km_out <- km_pooling(    x = wimids,    surv_formula = km_fit    ) #> ℹ Input: <wimids>: weighted datasets extracted with MatchThem::complete(action #>   = "all", all = FALSE, include = FALSE) (m = 5) #> ℹ Fitting Kaplan-Meier survival function with ggsurvfit::survfit2() in each #>   dataset: #>   formula: survival::Surv(fu_itt_months, death_itt) ~ treat #>   weights = weights (default for the input type) #>   robust = TRUE (derived: weights, cluster or id are used)   # median survival time  km_out$km_median_survival #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>   strata t_median t_lower t_upper #>   <fct>     <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> #> 1 0          16.8    14.0    19.6 #> 2 1          20.7    17.8    24.3   # KM curve  km_out$km_plot    # 2) list of data frames: weights are specified explicitly via `...`  # (all = FALSE excludes observations with zero weight)  datasets <- MatchThem::complete(wimids, action = "all", all = FALSE, include = FALSE)  km_out_list <- km_pooling(    x = datasets,    surv_formula = km_fit,    weights = weights    ) #> ℹ Input: list of data frames supplied by the user; no weights or cluster #>   applied automatically (m = 5) #> ℹ Fitting Kaplan-Meier survival function with ggsurvfit::survfit2() in each #>   dataset: #>   formula: survival::Surv(fu_itt_months, death_itt) ~ treat #>   weights = weights (specified by you) #>   robust = TRUE (derived: weights, cluster or id are used)   # for matched datasets, additionally specify the matched sets as clusters:  # km_pooling(x = datasets, surv_formula = km_fit, weights = weights, cluster = subclass)   # weights stored in a column with another name, e.g., `w`  datasets_w <- lapply(datasets, function(d) dplyr::rename(d, w = weights))  km_out_w <- km_pooling(    x = datasets_w,    surv_formula = km_fit,    weights = w    ) #> ℹ Input: list of data frames supplied by the user; no weights or cluster #>   applied automatically (m = 5) #> ℹ Fitting Kaplan-Meier survival function with ggsurvfit::survfit2() in each #>   dataset: #>   formula: survival::Surv(fu_itt_months, death_itt) ~ treat #>   weights = w (specified by you) #>   robust = TRUE (derived: weights, cluster or id are used)   # 3) imputed (mids) object: unweighted Kaplan-Meier curve  km_out_mids <- km_pooling(    x = mids,    surv_formula = km_fit    ) #> ℹ Input: <mids>: imputed datasets extracted with mice::complete(action = "all", #>   include = FALSE); unweighted (m = 5) #> ℹ Fitting Kaplan-Meier survival function with ggsurvfit::survfit2() in each #>   dataset: #>   formula: survival::Surv(fu_itt_months, death_itt) ~ treat #>   no weights, cluster or other arguments used   # 4) pass additional arguments to the underlying survfit2() call:  # column names are resolved in each imputed dataset, e.g. `id = patientid`.  # survfit() uses `id` as the subject identifier for its robust/sandwich  # variance calculation, clustering rows by patient instead of treating  # each row as its own independent cluster (relevant if a patient can  # contribute more than one row, e.g. with time-varying covariates).  km_out_id <- km_pooling(    x = wimids,    surv_formula = km_fit,    id = patientid    ) #> ℹ Input: <wimids>: weighted datasets extracted with MatchThem::complete(action #>   = "all", all = FALSE, include = FALSE) (m = 5) #> ℹ Fitting Kaplan-Meier survival function with ggsurvfit::survfit2() in each #>   dataset: #>   formula: survival::Surv(fu_itt_months, death_itt) ~ treat #>   weights = weights (default for the input type) #>   id = patientid (specified by you) #>   robust = TRUE (derived: weights, cluster or id are used)

code: library(encore.analytics)  library(mice)  library(dplyr) #>  #> Attaching package: ‘dplyr’ #> The following objects are masked from ‘package:stats’: #>  #>     filter, lag #> The following objects are masked from ‘package:base’: #>  #>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union  library(MatchThem)  library(survival)   # simulate a cohort with 1,000 patients with 20% missing data  data <- simulate_data(    n = 500,    imposeNA = TRUE,    propNA = 0.2    ) |>    # anesrake works best with factor variables    mutate(c_smoking_history = factor(ifelse(c_smoking_history == TRUE, "Current/former", "Never")))   # impute the data (create mids object)  set.seed(42)  mids <- mice(data, m = 5, print = FALSE) #> Warning: Number of logged events: 765   # define covariates for propensity score model  covariates <- data |>   select(starts_with("c_"), starts_with("dem_")) |>    colnames()   # define propensity score model  fit <- as.formula(paste("treat ~", paste(covariates, collapse = " + ")))   # match patients within each imputed dataset  mimids <- matchthem(    formula = fit,    datasets = mids,    approach = 'within',    method = 'nearest'    ) #>  #> Matching Observations  | dataset: #1 #> Warning: Fewer control units than treated units; not all treated units will get #> a match. #>  #2 #> Warning: Fewer control units than treated units; not all treated units will get #> a match. #>  #3 #> Warning: Fewer control units than treated units; Use suppressMessages() silence warning raised datasets contain weights subclass column used weights/cluster/id argument specified; specify weights = NULL cluster = NULL confirm columns ignored Column names passed weights, cluster id checked datasets informative error raised column exist documentation input types, default arguments argument precedence shared km_pooling() cox_pooling() extended examples input type km_pooling() now handles single dataset (m = 1, e.g., complete data without imputation list length one): since -imputation variance 0 definition, total variance set within-dataset variance warning raised. Previously, pool.scalar() returned NA total variance, standard errors, confidence intervals confidence interval median survival time NA misleading without warning Documented cited method used km_pooling() pool survival probabilities: Rubin’s rules complementary log-log transformation survival probability, log(-log(1 - S)), within-dataset variance obtained via delta method, described Morisot et al. (2015, BMC Med Res Methodol 15:54, https://doi.org/10.1186/s12874-015-0048-4) following recommendation Marshall et al. (2009, BMC Med Res Methodol 9:57, https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2288-9-57). calculation unchanged. documentation previously attributed transformation different publication (Marshall, Billingham, Bryan 2009), corrected. documentation now also states transformation applied S therefore differs log(-log(S)) used confidence intervals survival::survfit(conf.type = "log-log"): single dataset, point estimates standard errors agree survfit(), confidence intervals differ slightly Added cli Imports

title: encore.analytics 0.3.0
text: Added ... argument km_pooling() forwards additional arguments per-imputation ggsurvfit::survfit2() call (onwards survival::survfit()), e.g. type = "fleming-harrington". Arguments km_pooling() sets internally (formula, data, weights, cluster, robust) raise informative error supplied way Fixed shortcoming agreement_metrics() passing estimate_label "HR (95% CI)" (e.g. "(95% CI)" custom label) raised “object ‘footnote_label’ found” error; footnote now includes matching abbreviation recognized labels (“HR (95% CI)”, “(95% CI)”, “RR (95% CI)”) simply omits unrecognized labels Fixed bug agreement_metrics() significance_agreement report "Yes" even RWE confidence interval crossed null value 1 (.e. statistically significant), underlying check compared wrong confidence bound. classification rewritten categorize RCT RWE results independently position relative null (entirely , entirely , straddling ) require match; also fixes related gap “non-significant” agreement case recognized protective direction harmful direction Added metrics argument agreement_metrics() lets callers select agreement metrics (significance_agreement, estimate_agreement, smd_agreement) compute display; unselected metrics — notably expensive SMD calculation — skipped entirely rather computed hidden. Default remains three metrics, preserving existing behavior Added show_aggregate show_aggregate_total arguments agreement_metrics(). show_aggregate (default FALSE) adds summary row bottom table pooled agreement percentage displayed metric. show_aggregate_total (default TRUE) adds source note table single agreement percentage pooled across displayed metrics rows combined; exclude “NA” cells (e.g. failed SMD calculations) denominator. show_aggregate_total TRUE, pooled percentage also attached directly returned gt object (e.g. result$show_aggregate_total) programmatic access without parsing source note text Added smd_scale argument agreement_metrics() ("log" [default], "identity", "logit", "cloglog") controlling transform applied SMD calculation, since log-transforming (previous, hardcoded behavior) appropriate ratio-scale effect measures (HR, , RR, IRR). "identity" supports difference-scale measures (e.g. risk differences), "logit" supports proportions bounded [0, 1], "cloglog" (log-log transform survival probability, log(-log(p))) intended comparing survival probabilities scale survival::survfit()’s conf.type = "log-log" confidence interval method. (Correction: earlier version entry stated scale Kaplan-Meier estimates pooled km_pooling(); km_pooling() pools log(-log(1 - p)), see .) Note: smd_scale changes SMD transform — agreement_metrics()’s positivity check significance_agreement’s null value 1 still assume ratio-scale effect measure regardless smd_scale, known limitation non-ratio-scale effect sizes addressed change Added digits argument (default 2) agreement_metrics() rounds RCT/RWE estimates confidence limits agreement metric computed, e.g. RWE estimate 0.799 RCT confidence limit 0.80 agree; table displays rounded values digits decimals. digits = NULL disables rounding. agreement_metrics() now also validates inputs strictly: estimates must positive (checked rounding), interval must satisfy lower <= estimate <= upper, estimate/limit columns must numeric, smd_threshold must single positive number. Missing estimates limits now give "NA" agreement result (excluded pooled percentages) instead error misleading ""
